data.name: Maimun
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'A-M-M', meaning guarded, protected, secure. In the Islamic context, it is a name of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and Imam Ali (as).
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the concept of being under the protection of Allah.
data.numerology_meaning: People with this name are creative, artistic, and love beauty. They are also very generous and caring.

in_arabic.name: ميمون
in_arabic.long_meaning: ميمون هو اسم عربي مشتق من الفعل أمّن، ويُشتق من الجذر الأصلي ميم-واو-نون، ويتعلق بالرغبة والآمال والرزق والغنى، وقد استخدم في التاريخ الإسلامي لذكره في بعض الروايات النبوية الشريفة

in_urdu.name: میمون
in_urdu.long_meaning: میمون ایک عربی نام ہے جو فعل امن سے ماخوذ ہے، اور یہ جڑ ميم-و-نون سے اخذ کیا گیا ہے، جو رغبت، امیدیں، رزق اور دولت سے متعلق ہے، اور اس کا تذکرہ اسلامی تاریخ میں بعض احادیث میں ہوا ہے

in_hindi.name: मैमून
in_hindi.long_meaning: मैमून एक अरबी नाम है जो अम्न फعل से लिया गया है, और इसका मूल मिम-वा-नुन है, जो इच्छा, आशा, रोजी और धन से संबंधित है, और इसका उल्लेख इस्लामी इतिहास में कुछ हदीसों में हुआ है

in_pashto.name: میمون
in_pashto.long_meaning: ميمون د عربي نوم دی چې د امن فعل څخه اخستل شوی، او دا د ميم-و-نون څخه اخستل شوی، چې د هيلې، اميد، روزۍ او شتمنۍ سره اړخ لري، او دا په اسلامي تاريخ کې ځينو حديثو کې ذکر شوی

in_english.name: Maimun
in_english.long_meaning: Maimun is an Arabic name derived from the root amn, and it is related to blessings, desires, sustenance, and wealth, and it has been mentioned in some Islamic traditions and hadiths

data.cultural_impact: The name "Maimun" holds a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. It highlights a sense of protection, security, and comfort, which are essential elements of any loving and stable community. In the Middle Eastern and South Asian regions where Islamic identity is deeply rooted, the name is often given to children as a symbol of hope for a blessed, prosperous, and secure life.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Maimun" lies in its derivation from the Arabic root 'A-M-M', which is also found in many Quranic verses and Prophetic hadiths that emphasize God's protection and security of His devoted servants. This name is believed to be a reminder of God's promise to provide protection and create a secure environment for believers. So, carrying the name "Maimun" is not just a matter of personal identification but also a constant source of inspiration to seek God's protection and guidance throughout life. Additionally, it reflects the spiritual significance of the names of the revered figureheads in the Islamic history, such as Prophet Ibrahim and Imam Ali, who were themselves protectors and caretakers of their communities and the faith.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Maimun Rashid Al-Din, born in 1313 CE in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, was a Timurid ruler in the 14th century. He is known for patronizing scholars, artists and architects, transforming Samarkand into a major cultural center of the Islamic world.
